raw_record.question_text: Quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle. $m\angle 2 = 40$. Find $m\angle 6$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A is at the upper left, B lower left, C upper right, D lower right, with diagonals AD and BC drawn. Angle 2 is at A between vertical side AB and diagonal AD; angle 6 is at B between bottom side BD and diagonal BC. From the text, ABCD is a rectangle and m∠2 = 40. Use the rectangle right angle at B in triangle ABD: since ∠2 is 40 and triangle ABD is right at B, the angle at D between DB and DA, labeled ∠4, is 50. Then compare right triangles ABD and DCB: AB = CD as opposite sides of a rectangle, BD is common, and both have right angles, so the triangles are congruent. Therefore the angle at D in triangle ABD corresponds to the angle at B in triangle DCB, so ∠6 = ∠4 = 50.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the rectangle has horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides; diagonal AD goes from A to D and diagonal BC goes from B to C. Angle 2 is measured from the vertical side AB to diagonal AD, while angle 6 is measured from the horizontal side BD to diagonal BC. From the text, m∠2 = 40 and the figure is a rectangle. Let the rectangle have width w = BD and height h = AB = CD. In right triangle ABD, ∠2 is between the vertical height h and diagonal AD, so tan(40°) = w/h. In right triangle BCD, ∠6 is between the horizontal width w and diagonal BC, so tan(∠6) = h/w. Since h/w is the reciprocal of w/h, tan(∠6) = cot(40°) = tan(50°). Hence m∠6 = 50.
